title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Workforce Insights agent for leaders, managers and delegates
summary: Hold: the briefing implies that People Skills needs a separate licence, although Microsoft says it is included with Copilot or Viva licences. It also reports deployment and blocking automation as undocumented despite published package-management APIs, and incorrectly includes access policies among settings configurable through agent chat.

claims.claim: Automation for choosing the agent's deployment audience is not yet documented.
claims.quote:
acquireUsersAndGroups | packageAccessEntity collection | Users/groups for whom the package is deployed.
deployedTo | packageAcquireStatus | Enum value indicating the deployment scope of the package. Required if updating acquireUsersAndGroups.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to kind 'graph', call 'PATCH /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackagedetail-update'. Add to its note: 'Package deployment scope uses deployedTo and acquireUsersAndGroups; availability uses availableTo and allowedUsersAndGroups. This beta API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence and delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission; production use is not supported.' Replace the open question about absent pilot-limiting APIs with 'Does general availability change these beta package-management APIs?' Cite the package overview, which defines packages as agents or tools in the organisation catalog.

claims.fix: Set controls[1].api to kind 'graph', call 'POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackage-block'.
